page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-amd is a High Performance family virtual server configured with 4 shared vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, the hardware allocation consists of 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled and a 16 MB L3 cache. This instance includes 180 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address, with no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates moderate CPU capabilities alongside memory bandwidth constraints. The server achieves average tier performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations. However, memory performance drops significantly under larger workloads, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidths falling into the bottom 10% at 17.9 GB/sec and 12.56 GB/sec respectively. Similarly, Geekbench and Passmark scores place the instance in the weak to poor categories, reflecting its shared CPU allocation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU architecture and 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio position this server as a budget-friendly option for workloads requiring local NVMe storage without demanding sustained, dedicated compute power. It is suitable for light web serving, basic software compilation, development environments, and non-critical background tasks. It is less suited for high-throughput database operations or memory-intensive applications due to its lower memory bandwidth and shared resource model.
